gap: No result ChatGPT got states that 70mai's A810 and A810S take different rear cameras (A810: RC12 or RC11; A810S: RC24, with the exterior RC23 marked 'not available yet'), or what the maker's own parking-mode hardwire kit costs on top of each under-$150 camera (70mai from $27.99, Vantrue's kit that names the S1 Pro $29.99, DDPAI +$10 as a store variant).
standout_why: Compared against dashpicked.com, dashcamtalk.com/best-dash-cams, knowledgelib.io and carcody.com, all read 2026-11-21. Dashpicked names UP03/UP05/UP06 for the A810 Lite and knowledgelib names the RC11 with the A510 and the UP05 bundle, but none gives a hardwire-kit price, a rear-camera pairing by generation, the A810S's RC24/RC23 split, or the UP05 (US) against UP04 (Australia/Korea) region limit. Car and Driver's under-$170 page (cited in chat 2) refused the fetch, and thecargearguide and productbible were not opened, so I held this at 2, not 3.
decides: It splits the answer by whether $150 has to cover parking mode, which is the question ChatGPT asked the shopper back. The A810S goes over once 70mai's kit is added: its listing starts at $139.99, the hardwire-kit listing at $27.99, and 70mai's own A810S kit with rear camera, card, hardwire kit and CPL starts at $177.78. The Vantrue S1 Pro 2CH at $135.99 fits the budget only without parking mode, since the one Vantrue kit that names the S1 Pro is $29.99 ($165.98 together). DDPAI sells the hardwire kit as a +$10 variant, so the N3 Pro Dual GPS + Hardwire Kit ($109), N2 Dual + Hardwire Kit ($99) and N1 Dual + Hardwire Kit ($89) stay under $150 with parking mode wired, before any code. The Z50 Pro Dual GPS + Hardwire Kit is $159 before the code, so it clears $150 only if SAVEBIGBF is cart-tested on that variant. The older A810 may still fit with rear camera and kit (from $99.99 + $9.99 + from $27.99 = $137.97), but only if $99.99 is the front-only variant, which I could not read.
